fields.question: In a fictional early community, families prepare soil, plant seeds and care for growing crops. Which explanation best connects these activities with their livelihood?
fields.optionA: They use land and farming skills to produce food.
fields.optionB: They obtain fish by preparing the soil.
fields.optionC: They make pottery simply by planting seeds.
fields.optionD: They prove every community grows the same crops.
fields.explanation: Preparing soil and caring for crops are farming activities that help produce food. Communities used different resources and practices.
fields.learningPoint: Preparing soil and caring for crops are farming activities that help produce food. Communities used different resources and practices.
fields.historicalClue: Preparing soil and caring for crops are farming activities that help produce food. Communities used different resources and practices.

answerExplanations.A: Preparing soil and caring for crops are farming activities that help produce food. Communities used different resources and practices.
answerExplanations.B: The described activities concern crops rather than catching fish.
answerExplanations.C: Pottery requires different materials and craft skills.
answerExplanations.D: One community cannot establish what every community grew.

fields.question: A learning illustration shows a family tending a field and later storing its harvest. What conclusion is supported by both clues?
fields.optionA: Farming helped the family obtain food from cultivated crops.
fields.optionB: The family obtained all its food only through fishing.
fields.optionC: Every family across the islands planted identical crops.
fields.optionD: Harvesting meant the family no longer needed other resources.
fields.explanation: Tending a field and collecting its harvest show how farming could support food needs. The clues do not describe every family.
fields.learningPoint: Tending a field and collecting its harvest show how farming could support food needs. The clues do not describe every family.
fields.historicalClue: Tending a field and collecting its harvest show how farming could support food needs. The clues do not describe every family.

answerExplanations.A: Tending a field and collecting its harvest show how farming could support food needs. The clues do not describe every family.
answerExplanations.B: The clues show cultivation, not fishing.
answerExplanations.C: A single illustration cannot establish practices everywhere.
answerExplanations.D: One food source does not remove all other needs.

fields.question: A fictional coastal community has access to fishing grounds. People prepare suitable gear and learn local water conditions. Why could fishing be an important livelihood here?
fields.optionA: Living near water guarantees every fishing trip succeeds.
fields.optionB: People can use aquatic resources and skills to obtain food.
fields.optionC: Fishing requires no knowledge or preparation.
fields.optionD: A coastal location proves crops never reach the community.
fields.explanation: Access to aquatic resources and fishing knowledge could help people obtain food. Location alone does not guarantee success or exclude other livelihoods.
fields.learningPoint: Access to aquatic resources and fishing knowledge could help people obtain food. Location alone does not guarantee success or exclude other livelihoods.
fields.historicalClue: Access to aquatic resources and fishing knowledge could help people obtain food. Location alone does not guarantee success or exclude other livelihoods.

answerExplanations.A: Access does not guarantee a successful catch.
answerExplanations.B: Access to aquatic resources and fishing knowledge could help people obtain food. Location alone does not guarantee success or exclude other livelihoods.
answerExplanations.C: The scenario explicitly shows preparation and knowledge.
answerExplanations.D: People could also obtain crops through cultivation or exchange.

fields.question: A teaching scene shows fishers returning with a catch and families preparing fish for meals. Which relationship do these clues best illustrate?
fields.optionA: Fishing gave every community exactly the same way of life.
fields.optionB: A livelihood used available resources to help meet food needs.
fields.optionC: Only leaders benefited from all fishing activities.
fields.optionD: A catch proves the community never exchanged goods.
fields.explanation: The catch and meals connect fishing with food needs. Further evidence is needed to describe other groups or trade practices.
fields.learningPoint: The catch and meals connect fishing with food needs. Further evidence is needed to describe other groups or trade practices.
fields.historicalClue: The catch and meals connect fishing with food needs. Further evidence is needed to describe other groups or trade practices.

answerExplanations.A: One scene does not describe all communities.
answerExplanations.B: The catch and meals connect fishing with food needs. Further evidence is needed to describe other groups or trade practices.
answerExplanations.C: The clues do not show that only leaders benefited.
answerExplanations.D: Fishing and exchange could both support a community.

fields.question: A family needs a container for harvested grain. A craftsperson has clay and knows how to shape and fire pots. Which action best applies craftsmanship to the need?
fields.optionA: Leave the clay unused and wait for a container to appear.
fields.optionB: Assume any raw material becomes a pot without skilled work.
fields.optionC: Use the appropriate skills and materials to make a storage pot.
fields.optionD: Stop growing crops because the family needs a container.
fields.explanation: Craftsmanship combines knowledge, skills and materials to make useful objects. A suitable pot can help address the storage need.
fields.learningPoint: Craftsmanship combines knowledge, skills and materials to make useful objects. A suitable pot can help address the storage need.
fields.historicalClue: Craftsmanship combines knowledge, skills and materials to make useful objects. A suitable pot can help address the storage need.

answerExplanations.A: Waiting does not use the available skills and materials.
answerExplanations.B: Making a pot requires knowledge and work.
answerExplanations.C: Craftsmanship combines knowledge, skills and materials to make useful objects. A suitable pot can help address the storage need.
answerExplanations.D: Stopping cultivation does not solve storage for the harvest.

fields.question: In a fictional workshop, people weave plant fibers into baskets and shape clay into vessels. What do these activities have in common?
fields.optionA: They show all objects were made from the same material.
fields.optionB: They show finished objects appeared without learning.
fields.optionC: They transform suitable materials through skill into useful products.
fields.optionD: They prove every community made identical designs.
fields.explanation: Both activities use knowledge and skill to transform materials into useful goods. Materials and designs could vary.
fields.learningPoint: Both activities use knowledge and skill to transform materials into useful goods. Materials and designs could vary.
fields.historicalClue: Both activities use knowledge and skill to transform materials into useful goods. Materials and designs could vary.

answerExplanations.B: Skilled production involves learning and practice.
answerExplanations.C: Both activities use knowledge and skill to transform materials into useful goods. Materials and designs could vary.
answerExplanations.D: Examples from one workshop cannot establish identical designs everywhere.

fields.question: One community has extra grain and needs clay pots. Potters nearby need grain. They discuss exchanging some grain directly for pots. What makes this an example of barter?
fields.optionB: The exchange requires that money be used.
fields.optionC: Only the group receiving grain can benefit.
fields.optionD: Goods are exchanged directly for other goods.
fields.explanation: Barter means exchanging goods or services directly without using money in that exchange. Both groups can receive something they need.
fields.learningPoint: Barter means exchanging goods or services directly without using money in that exchange. Both groups can receive something they need.
fields.historicalClue: Barter means exchanging goods or services directly without using money in that exchange. Both groups can receive something they need.

answerExplanations.B: Money is not used in the proposed direct exchange.
answerExplanations.C: Both groups have stated needs that the exchange can address.
answerExplanations.D: Barter means exchanging goods or services directly without using money in that exchange. Both groups can receive something they need.

fields.question: A fisher and a basket maker agree to exchange some fish for a basket. No money is part of their agreement. Which description best explains the exchange?
fields.optionA: It is farming because the fish will be eaten.
fields.optionB: It is not an exchange because the products differ.
fields.optionC: It proves all historical trade happened without money.
fields.optionD: It is barter because goods are directly exchanged.
fields.explanation: This particular exchange is barter. One example does not establish how every historical exchange took place.
fields.learningPoint: This particular exchange is barter. One example does not establish how every historical exchange took place.
fields.historicalClue: This particular exchange is barter. One example does not establish how every historical exchange took place.

answerExplanations.A: Producing crops and exchanging fish are different activities.
answerExplanations.C: A direct exchange does not prove all trade had the same form.
answerExplanations.D: This particular exchange is barter. One example does not establish how every historical exchange took place.

fields.question: A fictional coastal community has extra fish but needs storage pots. Another community makes pots and wants fish. Why might trade help both?
fields.optionA: Trade makes their resources and skills identical.
fields.optionB: Each can obtain a needed product from the other.
fields.optionC: Trade means neither group needs to produce goods again.
fields.optionD: The community with pots must give them away without an agreement.
fields.explanation: Trade can connect communities with different resources and skills, helping each obtain goods it needs or values.
fields.learningPoint: Trade can connect communities with different resources and skills, helping each obtain goods it needs or values.
fields.historicalClue: Trade can connect communities with different resources and skills, helping each obtain goods it needs or values.

answerExplanations.A: Exchange does not make local resources identical.
answerExplanations.B: Trade can connect communities with different resources and skills, helping each obtain goods it needs or values.
answerExplanations.C: Ongoing needs can still require production.
answerExplanations.D: The situation describes a possible agreed exchange.

fields.question: A community produces woven goods but cannot obtain every useful material locally. Visitors offer goods from another place. Which reason best explains interest in trade?
fields.optionA: Visitors prove local skills have no value.
fields.optionB: Exchange can provide access to products not easily available locally.
fields.optionC: Trading forces every community to abandon its own livelihood.
fields.optionD: One visit proves all communities followed identical trading practices.
fields.explanation: Trade can extend access beyond local resources. Local products and skills can also contribute to an exchange.
fields.learningPoint: Trade can extend access beyond local resources. Local products and skills can also contribute to an exchange.
fields.historicalClue: Trade can extend access beyond local resources. Local products and skills can also contribute to an exchange.

answerExplanations.A: Local goods may be valuable to others.
answerExplanations.B: Trade can extend access beyond local resources. Local products and skills can also contribute to an exchange.
answerExplanations.C: Trade can occur alongside existing livelihoods.
answerExplanations.D: One encounter cannot describe all trading practices.
